//: Glass Atrium ~/.claude/settings.json PERMISSIONS template (DF-22 reference — NOT auto-applied).
DEFECT: an rm NEGATION placed inside permissions.allow — e.g. "!Bash(rm:*)" — is likely INERT.
Claude Code's permission layer denies via the permissions.deny array; an allow-list negation is
not the documented deny mechanism, so "Bash(*)" + "!Bash(rm:*)" in allow does NOT reliably block
rm at the permission layer (the block-dangerous-commands.sh hook is a SEPARATE, later gate).
FIX: declare rm rules in permissions.deny (below).
deny is evaluated first, then ask, then allow — first match wins (deny → ask → allow).
APPLY: merge ONLY the "permissions" object into your existing ~/.claude/settings.json (never wipe
other keys). wire_hooks (lib/ga-config-hooks.sh) never touches permissions, so this stays manual.
LIVE-VERIFY (see the "live_verify" key): confirm rm is blocked at the PERMISSION layer, not merely
by the dangerous-command hook.
HOOKS: the "hooks" block below documents the edit-time syntax gate (validate-edit-syntax.sh), a
PreToolUse(Write|Edit) advisory that runs bash -n / node --check / py_compile by extension allowlist.
It is advisory only (warns on a syntax error, never blocks) and
exempts templates. wire_hooks (from the ga-env.sh EXPECTED_HOOK_BINDINGS SoT) wires it automatically
with an absolute command path; this block is the manual-reference form.
ADVISORY(Bash): advisory-egress-secret.sh (H3) notes a credential-shaped literal co-occurring with an
outbound token in one command; advisory-raw-store-read.sh (H2) notes a Bash read of the wiki raw
store. Both are NON-BLOCKING (exit 0 always) — visibility only, never a gate; wire_hooks registers
them from the ga-env.sh EXPECTED_HOOK_BINDINGS SoT alongside the other bindings.
INLINE SHELLS: Bash(rm:*) anchors on the LEADING token only, so an rm wrapped in a shell or
interpreter re-parse (bash -c, eval, python3 -c) is not denied here; no wrapper row is denied.
A wrapped root or home wipe still meets the rm-wipe row of block-dangerous-commands.sh; any other
wrapped rm passes both layers.
NPM PUBLISH: Bash(npm publish:*) sits in permissions.ask — a user-approval gate (same shape as the LLM06
explicit-approval principle), not a hard deny. Leading-token matching: foo && npm publish / npx npm publish
do NOT match; a Layer-3 PreToolUse(Bash) command-string scan is a follow-up candidate, out of scope here.
REDIRECT INEXPRESSIBILITY (T21): 'a redirect INTO a harness path' (echo x > ~/.claude/hooks/y) is
INEXPRESSIBLE as a Bash(<prefix>:*) deny — the > operator and its path target appear anywhere in the
command, not as a leading prefix the matcher anchors on. No permission row blocks it: a write into
the harness is detected after the fact by the manifest comparison in glass-atrium doctor, never here.
live_verify: 1. Apply the permissions block above to ~/.claude/settings.json, then start a fresh 'claude' session.
2. Request an rm command, e.g. Bash: rm /tmp/ga-df22-probe
3. EXPECT: the call is DENIED at the permission layer (permission prompt / auto-deny), BEFORE any
hook fires. A pass = rm cannot execute. Contrast with the pre-fix state, where '!Bash(rm:*)' sat
inside permissions.allow and rm was NOT permission-denied (only the hook, if present, caught it).
4. Positive control: Bash: ls /tmp — MUST still be permitted (deny is scoped to rm only).
5. For the publish row: from a scratch package dir (package.json with private:true), request
Bash: npm publish --dry-run — EXPECT a permission PROMPT (ask), not an auto-deny: decline → not
executed, approve → executed. Positive control: Bash: npm ls — MUST still be permitted.
